clue.text: Freezing point transformed frozen contents

indicators.note: transformed tells us the letters picked out are rearranged into a new order
contents asks for the inside of the word frozen, everything but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Ice at freezing point has turned what was frozen into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' strips the F and N from FROZEN, leaving ROZE; 'transformed' rearranges those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: On the Celsius scale water freezes at nought degrees, so the freezing point is that figure.

clue.text: Cover ground after rousing talk that could make one dry up?

definitions.text: that could make one dry up?

indicators.note: rousing means getting up, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: to pave is to cover ground with a hard surface
an oration is a formal talk or speech

explanation.surface: After a stirring speech, someone gets to work laying paving.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'after rousing' (once got up) means the paving word is read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaporation is the process by which liquid disappears, so it is what makes a puddle dry up.

clue.text: Foreman goes around team leader to misjudge a corner

indicators.note: goes around says the supervisor's word wraps another letter

parts.note: an overseer is a foreman, a supervisor of workers

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of team

explanation.surface: A works foreman steers round the team captain while taking a bend badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Foreman looks like a name or a job title for the definition, but it is the wrapper; 'goes around' and 'leader' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A car oversteers when it turns more sharply than intended, a driving error on a bend.

clue.text: Feign death in tree, so a spy gets confused

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the tree's name

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree

indicators.note: gets confused tells us the letters of so a spy are scrambled

explanation.surface: A spy hiding up a tree pretends to be dead and loses track of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feign death' is the definition; 'in' and 'gets confused' work on the rest, the spy's letters scrambled inside a fruit tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To play possum is an idiom for pretending to be dead, as the opossum does when threatened.

clue.text: Lead poisoning's highest on sports ground and garden, mostly

indicators.note: highest in a down clue means the top letter of poisoning's

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground for sport

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden

explanation.surface: Lead poisoning was worst near the sports field and much of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead is the verb, to go first, not the metal of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to go before, so it is a synonym of lead in the sense of walking in front.

clue.text: Payee came on start of programme after dithering hosts managed to provide this?

definitions.text: Payee came on start of programme after dithering hosts managed to provide this?

indicators.note: hosts means the jumbled letters hold another word inside
after dithering suggests indecisive wavering, so the letters are scrambled
start of asks for the first letter of programme

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A performer who turned up on a show is paid simply for being there.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay together: 'after dithering' scrambles the letters and 'hosts' tucks in the word for managed.
explanation.definitionFit: Appearance money is a fee paid to a celebrity or athlete just for turning up at an event.

clue.text: Wall's top mimic, getting into character

indicators.note: getting into says one word goes inside another

parts.note: a part is a character played by an actor
to ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: An impressionist gets into character atop a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a roof or bridge, so it tops a wall.

clue.text: Hot story from singular pen

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a coop is a pen for poultry

explanation.surface: A sensational news story comes from one writer's pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is an exclusive news story that a paper gets ahead of its rivals.

clue.text: Mix gallons in pool

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the word for pool

parts.note: a mere is a small lake or pool

explanation.surface: Gallons of liquid are mixed into a pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge is to combine or blend things together, a synonym of mix.

clue.text: Goalie who's up for it might be one of Rangers

parts.note: someone who is game is willing, up for it
a goalie is a goalkeeper, or keeper for short

explanation.surface: A keen goalkeeper might play for Glasgow Rangers football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers looks like the Scottish football club; here it means countryside wardens.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamekeeper is a kind of ranger, a warden who looks after land and the wildlife on it.

clue.text: Time is hard for us

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
something for us is ours, belonging to us

explanation.surface: Time is a tough business for people like us.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour is a unit of time, sixty minutes long, so it serves as an example.

clue.text: From America's point of view, the French mess up

parts.note: from the point of view of the US is read as to US, i.e. to us
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: Americans think the French make a hash of things, with the ellipsis leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: America is read as US, and 'to us' means from our point of view, so the phrase gives TO US.
explanation.definitionFit: To tousle is to make untidy, especially hair, so it is a synonym of disorder.

clue.text: … typically American tarte Tatin, for example

definitions.meaning: the saying 'as American as' the pudding means thoroughly American
tarte Tatin is an upside-down French apple tart, a kind of fruit pastry dish

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue's surface about the French; tarte Tatin is a caramelised upside-down tart.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom ties the pudding to Americanness, and a tarte Tatin is a fruit tart baked in pastry.

clue.text: Something to get pests removed, locked up, shackling like a mad'ouse?

indicators.note: shackling means one word is held inside another

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison
a madhouse is hectic; the apostrophe drops the H, as in Cockney speech, giving the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a chaotic jail wants something to deal with the vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in mad'ouse signals the dropped H, so hectic loses its first letter; 'shackling' holds that inside the prison slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: An insecticide is a chemical used to kill insects, getting rid of pests.

clue.text: Many a lecture is sampled here

indicators.note: sampled says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: This is a place where students hear many lectures.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an American university, a place where lectures are given, so 'here' points to it in an all-in-one reading.

clue.text: Backing price reduction, cities arranged to make things stretch

indicators.note: Backing means the word for a price cut is read from right to left

parts.note: a sale is a time of reduced prices

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of cities are put into a new order

explanation.surface: City councils back a price cut while organising stretchy goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns SALE into ELAS; 'arranged' shuffles CITIES into TICISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elasticise is to make a fabric or material stretchy by adding elastic.

clue.text: Painting company having a gloomy aspect

parts.note: to lour is to look dark and threatening, so louring means gloomy-looking

explanation.surface: A firm of painters is having a depressing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Colouring is the act of applying colour, which is painting in its simplest sense.

clue.text: Critic scuffling with a hero leaves a sour taste in the mouth

definitions.text: leaves a sour taste in the mouth

indicators.note: scuffling suggests a jumbled tussle, so the letters of Critic are mixed up

parts.note: El Cid was the Castilian hero of medieval Spain

explanation.surface: A reviewer brawls with a celebrated hero and is left feeling bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Citric acid gives lemons and other citrus fruits their sharp sourness on the tongue.

clue.text: Some morris dancers are so choked up

definitions.meaning: morris dancers in the north of England dance in wooden clogs, so they are wearing clogs
blocked or obstructed, as a drain is

explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance; some troupes wear clogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A clogged drain is blocked, and a person shod in clogs, like some morris dancers, is also described this way.

clue.text: Hate having short drinks tipped in river

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales

indicators.note: tipped means the drink word is upended, read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: sips are small drinks

explanation.surface: Someone loathes having their small measures poured into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' upends the drinks, read upwards in this down clue, before they go into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To despise someone is to feel contempt and loathing for them, a synonym of hate.

clue.text: Get stuck in Strand

definitions.meaning: to jam fast, as wheels do when they seize
a single tress or curl of hair

explanation.definitionFit: Wheels lock when they jam, and a lock is also a tress or strand of hair.

clue.text: American crawler software infiltrating network on Scottish island

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island
a worm is malicious software that spreads through a computer network

explanation.surface: A computer virus invades a network based on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch (from Gaelic innis) is used in Scottish place names for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: The looper caterpillar of geometrid moths is called this in North America, a crawling larva.

clue.text: I percolate away, briefly concerned with part of intestine

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to leach is to drain away by liquid seeping through

explanation.surface: A person describes coffee percolating as quickly as they can.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileac is the adjective relating to the ileum, the last section of the small intestine.

clue.text: Sentimental stuff overwhelms one boy

indicators.note: overwhelms says the first word engulfs another

parts.note: corn is trite sentimental material
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Mawkish material overpowers a single lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Corin is a male given name, the old shepherd in Shakespeare's As You Like It.

clue.text: Film company boss with heart of lion

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob or ornament

indicators.note: heart of asks for the middle letters of the word lion

explanation.surface: A movie studio chief with a lion-hearted nature, perhaps MGM's roaring lion.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss here is the ornamental knob, not the manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a film-making company, as in the big Hollywood studios.

clue.text: Nobleman almost ahead of his time

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: someone ahead of time is early

explanation.surface: A forward-thinking aristocrat was nearly a man before his time.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer, a rank of the nobility below marquess.

clue.text: Soldier visiting in the wars gets trench mouth

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: in the wars means battered and knocked about, so the letters of visiting are jumbled

explanation.surface: A soldier visiting the front line picks up a mouth infection from the trenches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wars' rearranges VISITING into NGIVITIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trench mouth is an acute form of gum inflammation, named from its prevalence among First World War soldiers.

clue.text: Years immersed in deception with excellent Spanish mystery writer

parts.note: a con is a trick or deception
and means together with

indicators.note: immersed in puts one piece inside the rest

parts.note: ole is the Spanish cry of approval, bravo

explanation.surface: A Spanish crime novelist spent years deep in trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: Ole is the Spanish cheer of approval, the equivalent of bravo; 'immersed in' sinks the years abbreviation into the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Conan Doyle created Sherlock Holmes, making him a celebrated author of detective mysteries.

clue.text: Dull note in margins of galley

indicators.note: in puts the musical note inside the picked letters
margins of picks the first and last letters of galley

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A dull note scribbled in the margins of a printer's galley proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes something dreary and lacking interest, a synonym for dull.
